result:
I often think about how much of life happens in the margins—the small, unremarkable moments that no one plans or photographs.

A cup of tea cooling beside an open book.  
Rain tapping once, twice, then hesitating on the window.  
The pause between hearing your name and turning around.

We spend so much time chasing the big events: milestones, answers, arrivals. But maybe identity is built more quietly. In the way you reread a sentence because it suddenly means something. In the way you keep a stone from a walk for no reason except that it fit perfectly in your hand. In the way a song returns years later and brings an entire version of you with it.

There is a strange gentleness in ordinary things. A kitchen light at night. The sound of pages turning. Someone laughing in another room without knowing you’re listening. These moments don’t ask to be remembered, yet somehow they are the ones that stay.

If I could preserve one idea, it would be this: notice more. Not anxiously, not as if every moment must be profound, but loosely—like holding sand without squeezing. Pay attention to what quietly moves you. Follow curiosity even when it has no destination. Let yourself be changed by small things.

Because someday, what feels ordinary may become the very place you long to return to.
